bio: Steep volcanic cone in western Haʻapai with a summit caldera, reached by hired boat and a one-hour climb.
Haʻapai volcano joined to Kao by an undersea ridge, with a steep one-hour climb to views of the crater.
Volcanic island in western Haʻapai where a steep hour's climb leads to the crater rim and views of Kao.
Almost uninhabited sand-cay island in Lifuka district with clean, quiet beaches and five small resorts.
Quiet sand-cay island beside Lifuka, almost uninhabited, with clean beaches and a few small resorts.
Almost empty sand-cay island in Haʻapai, reached by boat, with quiet beaches and five small resorts.
Tonga's northernmost island, a volcanic rim enclosing two crater lakes, where you hike the craters and swim.
Remote ring-shaped volcanic island at Tonga's far north, with freshwater crater lakes and the Tongan megapode.
Tonga's northernmost island, a volcanic ring around two crater lakes, with crater hikes and freshwater swims.
Freshwater crater lake at the heart of Niuafoʻou, 23 m above sea level, with four islands inside.
Niuafoʻou's central crater lake, the Big Lake, ringed by forested inner walls and reached with local guides.
Freshwater lake filling Niuafoʻou's crater, with four small islands, one visible only when the water drops.
The Sacred Island, a volcanic island in Tonga's far north with white beaches, lagoons and three villages.
Small volcanic island with white sand beaches, a freshwater spring dip and a climb to views of Tafahi's cone.
Tonga's far-north Sacred Island, with lagoon beaches, thatched fales and a steady climb to its high point.
Tiny island with a perfect 656 m volcanic cone, a steep climb, and Samoa visible on a fine day.
Small island north of Niuatoputapu, home to one village and a cone-shaped volcano you climb with a guide.
Cone-shaped volcanic island nine kilometres from Niuatoputapu, reached by outboard, with a steep summit climb.
